BACKGROUND

On June 14, 2023 the City Council approved the Operating and Capital Budget
for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. As part of the Capital Equipment component of the
budget, the Council approved $310,000 for the purchase of self-contained
breathing apparatus for all sworn personnel (SCBA) and an SCBA fill station.

SCBA are critical personal protective equipment for firefighters entering
environments that pose a threat to health and life safety. Standards for self-
contained breathing apparatus are governed by the National Fire Protection
Association (NFPA). The department’s current SCBA equipment was purchased
in 2011, have reached the end of their service life, and are two cycles out of
compliance with current NFPA standards. The department is seeking to replace
19 SCBAs and 60 cylinders, and install a fill station for SCBA maintenance.

In accordance with San Marino Municipal Code (SMMC) 02.06.05.B.5, all
purchases of goods and services greater than $30,000 require approval by the
City Council. The Fire Department will present the request for approval to
purchase the SCBAs and fill station at the December 13, 2023 City Council
meeting.

  PAGE 5 of 73
 DISCUSSION

The 3M Scott Air-Pak X3 Pro is an industrial/occupational SCBA. Each SCBA
consists of a full facepiece assembly; a removable, positive pressure, mask-
mounted regulator with air-saver switch; an automatic dual path redundant
pressure reducer; end-of-service time indicators; a harness and backframe
assembly for supporting the equipment on the body of the wearer; a shoulder
strap mounted, remote gauge indicating cylinder pressure; a rapid
intervention crew/universal air connection (RIC/UAC); a personal alert safety
system (PASS); and cylinder and valve assembly for storing breathing air
under pressure.

The 3M Scott SCBA is widely used by agencies throughout Area C, including
our immediate neighbors, the South Pasadena Fire Department (SPFD); and
the Pasadena Fire Department (PFD). Selecting 3M Scott SCBA provides the
continuing opportunity for the San Marino Fire Department to
exchange personnel, consistent with the Shared Personnel Agreement with
the SPFD. Interoperability of breathing apparatus equipment is essential to
safe and effective inter-changeability between the two agencies. If a different
product were purchased by the SMFD, sharing of personnel would not be
possible. It is in the best interests of the City to dispense with competitive
bidding and purchase the 3M Scott Air-Pak X3 Pro SCBAs. Allstar Fire
Equipment is the sole distributor for 3M Scott SCBA.

The Stallion Air Centaur 2G2 is an SCBA fill station that is used to refill SCBA
cylinders. The Stallion Air Centaur is the only product of its type with
automatic fill capability which provides for hands free, one button filling
without requiring an attendant to stand by until the bottles are filled. Stallion
fill stations are sold by L.N. Curtis under a cooperative purchasing agreement
through Sourcewell Contract 040220-LNC.

SUBJECT: SELECTION OF ATLAS PLANNING SOLUTIONS FOR LOCAL

STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

Efficient, Responsive, and Effective City Services
Fiscally Responsible and Transparent City Government
Safe Community

BACKGROUND

The Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000 (DMA2000) established a national program
for pre-disaster mitigation, which provides federal funding for projects that
are not dependent on a presidential disaster declaration and streamlines the
administration of disaster relief. In order to be eligible for federal disaster
relief, DMA2000 requires that local agencies conduct a disaster mitigation
planning process that includes drafting of a local hazard mitigation plan
(LHMP) for addressing:

  •  Cost effective actions for risk reduction that are agreed upon by
  stakeholders and the public;
  •  Providing resources for the greatest risks and vulnerabilities;
  •  Building partnerships involving residents, organizations, and
  businesses;
  •  Education and awareness of hazards and risks; and
  •  Communicating priorities to state and federal officials.

In addition, this process is used to identify policies and actions that can be
implemented over the long term to reduce risk and future losses. LHMPs form

  PAGE 13 of 73
 the foundation for a community’s long-term strategy to reduce disaster losses
and break the cycle of disaster damage, reconstruction, and repeated
damage. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) requires
LHMPs to address hazards, vulnerability and risk to be eligible for future FEMA
mitigation grant funds and reimbursement of disaster related expenses.

State and local governments must prepare and adopt an update to federally
approved LHMPs that comply with FEMA requirements every five years. The
City of San Marino’s current LHMP was prepared by Soteria Emergency
Management. The LHMP was adopted in 2019 and will expire in 2024.

DISCUSSION

The San Marino Fire Department published a Request for Proposals (RFP) on
the City’s website and on the PlanetBids procurement portal on October 4,
2023. Additionally, invitations were sent by mail to a list of recommended
vendors compiled by the Area C Disaster Management Coordinator. The RFP
was open for one month and was closed on November 3, 2023.

The Fire Department received proposals from eleven vendors in response to
the RFP. The proposals were reviewed by Fire Department staff and evaluated
based on the vendor’s background and experience, description of
services, project schedule, and cost proposal.

Of the eleven proposals received, R.E. Patterson and Associates and Atlas
Planning Solutions presented proposals that offered the most competitive
combination of previous LHMP experience, scope of services, and cost. The
Fire Department contacted references and reviewed samples of LHMPs that
each vendor had prepared for other agencies. Ultimately, the Fire Department
concluded that Atlas Planning Solutions will provide the best overall value of
experience, services, and cost.

  PAGE 14 of 73
 Atlas Planning Solutions (APS) is a woman-owned, and service-disabled
veteran-owned business located in Riverside, CA. APS specializes in the
integration of planning tools like Local Hazard Mitigation Plans and Climate
Adaptation Vulnerability Assessments into the General Plan. APS staff have
completed or are currently working on several LHMPs throughout the state
and has extensive experience assisting communities as they address the
changing legislative requirements and frameworks governing hazards and
resiliency within California. References for previous LHMP experience include
the City of Ontario, City of Anaheim, City of Irvine, and City of Huntington
Beach.

The Fire Department will request City Council approval to enter a professional
services agreement with Atlas Planning Solutions at the December 13, 2023
meeting of the City Council. If an agreement is approved, APS services would
commence immediately upon receiving notification to proceed. The term of
the agreement shall be from commencement until the LHMP is signed off with
FEMA, CalOES and adopted by the San Marino City Council. APS anticipates a
9-to-10-month schedule with a projected completion date in September
2024.

San Marino Fire Department 100th Anniversary
Over 250 attendees visited the fire station on Saturday to celebrate 100 years
of the San Marino Fire Department. Visitors to the open house were treated
to a tour of the fire station, historical exhibits, emergency preparedness and

participated in a Great Shake Out training exercise for earthquake
readiness. The exercise included a simulation of a significant earthquake in
Southern California and was led by the former Los Angeles Fire Department
Interim Fire Chief and General Manager of the City of Los Angeles’ Emergency
Management Department Jim Featherstone. City staff routinely participates in
emergency preparedness exercises to prepare staff to assist residents in an
emergency. The San Marino Fire Department offers quarterly emergency

BACKGROUND

Please accept the following as a summary of notable activities that have been
accomplished, are underway or are planned for the balance of this month
through your next regularly scheduled commission meeting.

DISCUSSION

Follow-up Items from Prior Commission Meetings
· The Public Works Department is working in conjunction with the Police
Department and the City’s on-call traffic engineering firm to begin evaluation
of the Traffic Task Force’s recommendations at select locations throughout the
City. Staff has identified three locations for the traffic engineering consultant
to evaluate for potential improvements. The traffic engineer has also begun
review and evaluation of existing signage, striping, and pavement legends
within the school zones at Valentine Elementary, Huntington Middle School,
San Marino High School, and Carver Elementary School.

· After the completion of a playground safety audit by a licensed playground
inspector earlier this year, it was determined a full-scale replacement of the
Lacy Park playground is recommended in the near future. Staff has met with
three playground design firms for presentations on their playground

  PAGE 65 of 73
 equipment and potential concepts for the playground replacement. Staff is
awaiting submittal of additional design concepts and cost proposals from each
firm. Presentations to the Playground Committee will be scheduled prior to
bringing the item to the City Council to request the appropriation of additional
funds for the project as part of the FY 24-25 budget.

Projects in or near Construction
· The FY 21-22 Street Rehabilitation Program project has been completed.
Staff will present the project’s Notice of Completion for City Council approval
at its December 13th meeting. As part of the project, 31 City streets were
resurfaced based upon the Council-adopted Pavement Management Plan
(PMP). In addition, the project also replaced over 13,000 linear feet of curb
and gutter as well as replacement of striping on the re-surfaced streets, and
the new re-striping of Sierra Madre Boulevard.

· The City’s Annual Sidewalk Replacement Program began in late July with all
replacements completed by early September. The punch list is now complete
and the City Council approved the Notice of Completion at its October 27th
meeting. In total, nearly 30,000 square feet of 4-inch sidewalk, 6-inch
sidewalk, curb and gutter, and driveway approaches were replaced at various
locations throughout the City. The next cycle of sidewalk replacement is
anticipated to begin in the Spring.

· Construction activities for the San Marino Center Renovation project are
substantially complete with the completion of final punch list items ongoing.
The public grand opening and ribbon cutting of the newly renovated facility
was held on Thursday, September 28th and was well-attended by members
of the community.

Projects in Design/Out-to-Bid
· At its June 30th meeting, the City Council approved the appropriation of
funding to complete repairs to the electrical, plumbing, and boiler and HVAC
systems at the Stoneman facility. These needed repairs will ensure that the
facility is able to remain operational and safe for short-term use by staff and
community members. Staff is currently preparing the bid packages and will
begin soliciting bids for the work in the coming weeks.

· A contract amendment for the upgrade of the City’s three sanitary sewer lift
stations was approved at the May 10th City Council meeting to increase the
project’s design budget to incorporate additional scope previously excluded by
former staff during preliminary design into the final plans. Dudek Engineers
completed the revisions to the plans and submitted the revised 100% design
package. Bids were recently received for the project with the awards of
contract scheduled for the December 13th City Council meeting.

 · At its September 13th meeting, the City Council approved a contract
amendment for Dudek Engineers, which amended their scope of work for the
Lacy Park Culvert replacement project. This new scope will evaluate
alternative storm drain alignments to re-route the storm drain in public streets
in order to help mitigate the project’s impact on Lacy Park.

· NCE recently submitted the 95% design plans for the next cycle of street
rehabilitation work, expected to begin later this fiscal year. The preliminary
list of streets were selected based on the Council-adopted Pavement
Management Plan (PMP), which provides a framework for street repaving
based on existing conditions and available funding.

· Staff is currently preparing the bid package for the Streetlight Replacement
Program to go out to bid this month. This project will replace metal streetlight
standards that are remaining on a few City streets with newer concrete
streetlight standards installed throughout the majority of the City.
